name: Canny
subcategory: feedback boards, interviews and product research
tagline: Collect feature requests, merge duplicates, publish statuses, and maintain a roadmap

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 25 tracked users; 5 managers; unlimited contributors, feedback and boards.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Starts at 100 tracked users; 10 managers; unlimited contributors.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Starts at 5,000 tracked users; custom managers, security, integrations and service terms.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 25 tracked users; 5 managers; unlimited contributors, feedback and boards.
pricing.billingTerms: Monthly + annual; the public Pro card exposes the annual-equivalent rate and says annual billing saves 20%; Business is custom.
pricing.hiddenCosts: Without a spend cap, exceeding the tracked-user band can automatically move the account to the next tier and create a prorated charge; with a spend cap, Canny stops tracking new users. Autopilot users count toward tracked-user usage.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Canny, collect feature requests, merge duplicates, publish statuses, and maintain a roadmap. The hard boundary is customer identity, integrations, changelog, prioritization, and team workflow, plus participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Collect structured feature requests, merge duplicates, connect evidence to themes, and publish a transparent roadmap with statuses.
whatYouLose: customer identity, integrations, changelog, prioritization, and team workflow
moatNotes: participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration
ongoingBurden: recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Canny because people pay either for access to participants or for a research repository that keeps evidence usable across an organization. The recurring cost buys recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Fider
priorArt.desc: Open-source customer-feedback portal with voting and status workflows.

alternatives.name: ClearFlask
alternatives.desc: Feedback, duplicate merging and a real roadmap; deployment is the least lightweight part.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose with the project's bundled dependencies
facts.dataFormat: In a self-hosted deployment the source-of-truth records live in a DynamoDB-compatible store, search/filter indexes live in MySQL/MariaDB or Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, and uploads live in S3-compatible storage; the bundled Compose profile persists these services under the deployment's data directory. The hosted edition keeps the equivalent data in ClearFlask's cloud.
facts.gapVsPaid: ClearFlask covers the feedback loop, but its AWS-shaped dependency stack, rougher administration, and smaller integration and support ecosystem are a substantial downgrade from Canny's managed product.
facts.setupBlocker: The simple Compose command starts a large dependency stack; a public deployment still needs environment configuration, a domain/TLS, outbound email, backups, and several stateful services.

alternatives.name: Quackback
alternatives.desc: Canny's whole loop in one Compose file, including duplicate merging; young, fast-moving, and worth pinning.

facts.dataFormat: Feedback posts, votes, comments, users, roadmap items, and changelog entries live in the deployment's PostgreSQL database; uploaded assets and generated files remain in the Docker-hosted storage configured by the deployment.
facts.gapVsPaid: Quackback implements posts, votes, duplicate merging, roadmap, and changelog, but it is younger, self-host-only, and far less proven in integrations, moderation, analytics, and support than Canny.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert must supply environment secrets, run and update Docker Compose, expose the service behind HTTPS, configure email, and back up its database.

alternatives.name: Sleekplan Indie
alternatives.desc: Unlimited feedback, a roadmap and a changelog for one admin; branding and the default workflow are the rent.

facts.install: Hosted signup, then embed the widget or publish the hosted feedback portal
facts.dataFormat: Feedback, votes, comments, roadmap items, changelog posts, user records, and widget configuration live in Sleekplan's cloud; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: Sleekplan's free plan is limited to one administrator and visible branding, with advanced workflow, segmentation, integrations, and customization behind paid plans.
facts.setupBlocker: There is no technical install hurdle, but the free Indie plan is limited to one administrator, carries Sleekplan branding, and reserves deeper workflow and customization controls for paid plans.

alternatives.name: UserJot
alternatives.desc: Two free feedback boards, duplicate detection, statuses and a public roadmap with no user meter hiding nearby.

facts.install: Hosted signup, create a board, and optionally add the widget or identify users
facts.dataFormat: Feedback, votes, comments, statuses, roadmap and changelog entries, user identity data, and configuration live in UserJot's cloud; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: UserJot is unusually complete for free, but its younger product and smaller ecosystem do not match Canny's mature integrations, enterprise controls, analytics, and support.
facts.setupBlocker: Setup is clean, but the permanent free plan is bounded to two boards and omits paid branding, domain, segmentation, and advanced administration options.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a small-team feedback repository DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Canny in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: collect structured feature requests, merge duplicates, connect evidence to themes, and publish a transparent roadmap with statuses.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create public and private feedback intake with consent text and optional contact details.
Support posts, votes, comments, tags, statuses, owners, and duplicate merging.
Add a research note type with evidence links, quotes, themes, and confidence.
Build search and filters across feedback, customers, segments, themes, and status.
Provide email notifications, moderation, export, deletion, and an audit log.
Publish a read-only roadmap or findings page using only explicitly public items.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out a paid research-participant marketplace.
Deliberately leave out unlimited video storage and automated transcription.
Deliberately leave out enterprise repositories, SSO, and governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
